# Difference of balls, one-limb center, finite core

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone2/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `ball_sub_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

A ball $Z$, of center $c_z$ and radius $r_z$, that contains $x - y$ for every $x \in X, y \in Y$, with $X$ the ball of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$ and $Y$ the ball of center $c_y$ and radius $r_y$.

$$Z \supseteq \{\, x - y : x \in X, y \in Y \,\}.$$

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet. The operations of the public headers call [`ball_sub_1_full`](ball_sub_1_full.md), which computes this kernel and then the fix-up of its results.

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $r_x \ge 0$.
- $r_y \ge 0$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $\lvert (x - y) - c_z\rvert \le r_z$ for all real $x$ and $y$ with $\lvert x - c_x\rvert \le r_x$, $\lvert y - c_y\rvert \le r_y$.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `ball_sub_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/Ball2.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/Ball2.v), against `ball_sub_1_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions ball_sub_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition ball_sub_1_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (1 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall cx rx cy ry : R,
  fmt emin prec cx ->
  fmt emin prec rx ->
  fmt emin prec cy ->
  fmt emin prec ry ->
  0 <= rx ->
  0 <= ry ->
  let '(cz, rz) := ball_sub_1 emin prec tie_even cx rx cy ry in
  fmt emin prec cz /\
  fmt emin prec rz /\
  (forall x y : R, Rabs (x - cx) <= rx -> Rabs (y - cy) <= ry -> Rabs ((x - y) - cz) <= rz).
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `ball_sub_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** midpoint-radius difference (Milestone 1 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_sub_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_sub_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`ball_add_1`](ball_add_1.md).

```
# The difference of two balls with one-limb centers: ball_add_1 with the second center negated.

n        = neg(cy)
(cz, rz) = ball_add_1(cx, rx, n, ry)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#ball_sub_1)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.

| Run | Cases judged | Failed | smallest slack of the radius, in gaps |
|---|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 6 634 872 | 0 | 1.25 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 6 628 662 | 0 | 1.25 |
| toy formats, every operand: 6 domains of 6 formats | 19 271 921 | 0 | 1 (`fp:3:-4:2`) |

The slack is how far the returned radius is above the smallest radius that encloses the exact set, in units in the last place of the radius: below 1, a radius one unit smaller would not enclose it.

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: [`ball_sub_1_full`](ball_sub_1_full.md) states that ([What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values) says what the library does now).
